title: Planted q-ary Noisy Parity-Check Likelihood Bridge: Exact Weight-Power Fourier Damping, Off-Dual Noise Invariance, and Dual Minimum-Distance Scaling

theorems.name: Exact Weight-Power Law for Classical Noisy Planted Subspace Characters
theorems.statement: Under i.i.d. q-ary depolarizing noise of rate gamma in [0, 1] on a dimension-d subspace B in F_q^n, E_(b ~ B, e ~ D_gamma^n)[omega_q^(<u, b + e>)] equals (1 - gamma)^(wt_H(u)) for u in B^perp and 0 for u not in B^perp.

theorems.name: Off-Dual Noise Invariance and On-Dual Weight-Stratified Window Acceptance
theorems.statement: For any window W in F_q of size R, p_W(u | B, gamma) = R/q for all u not in B^perp and all gamma in [0, 1], whereas for u in B^perp, p_W(u | B, gamma) = R/q + (1 - gamma)^(wt_H(u)) * (1_(0 in W) - R/q).

theorems.name: Dual Minimum-Distance Bias Frontier
theorems.statement: For any gamma in (0, 1), the distinguishing bias |p_W(u | B, gamma) - R/q| over non-zero probes u in F_q^n \ {0} is maximized at minimum-weight dual checks wt_H(u) = d^perp(B) = min_(v in B^perp \ {0}) wt_H(v), where it equals (1 - gamma)^(d^perp(B)) * |1_(0 in W) - R/q|.

implemented_field: prime fields only; integer residues are not extension-field arithmetic

physical_source_laws.coherent_random_translation: E_e X^e |B><B| X^-e gives QFT probability 1/|B^perp| on B^perp and zero elsewhere, independently of the translation distribution
physical_source_laws.coherent_translation_and_phase_noise: Adding independent Z^f phase noise with iid coordinate replacement rate gamma convolves the uniform dual distribution with the phase-error law
physical_source_laws.incoherent_classical_samples: The diagonal density operator of ANY classical sample distribution gives a uniform QFT output on the entire ambient space
physical_source_laws.counterexample: All three sources above have identical computational marginals for the controls. Classical sample characters alone do not specify a coherent source or its QFT probabilities.

retracted_claim: The v1 note incorrectly assigned the phase-noise convolution formula to a mixture of translated coherent coset states. Translation changes Fourier phases, not Fourier probabilities.
proof_obligations: Specify the actual joint density operator, environment and available registers before using a Fourier-noise formula
Supply and cost a coherent unknown-subspace source; explicit generator matrices here are calibration inputs, not a hidden-subspace algorithm
Do not infer a quantum state preparation or its inverse from a classical noisy sampler
Prove any noise law for the actual reduction, including correlations; iid coordinate noise is only a conditional model here
